holidays.name: National Banana Bread Day
holidays.description: A day devoted to the glorious art of turning overripe, brown-spotted bananas into a warm, moist loaf. Bakers everywhere celebrate by rescuing sad fruit from the counter and slathering the results with butter.
holidays.origin: Banana bread rose to popularity in the 1930s during the Great Depression, when thrifty home bakers refused to waste overripe bananas and baking powder and baking soda became widely available. The day itself is an unofficial food observance popularized by food-holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: Banana bread became a staple of American cookbooks after Pillsbury's 1933 cookbook included a recipe, and it later became a pandemic-era baking sensation in 2020.

holidays.name: National Dog Biscuit Day
holidays.description: A treat-filled celebration for your four-legged best friend. Pet owners hand out crunchy biscuits, and some brave souls bake their own homemade versions with peanut butter and pumpkin.
holidays.origin: Dog biscuits trace back to 1860s England, when James Spratt, an American electrician in London, saw dogs gobbling leftover ship biscuits and created the first commercial dog biscuit. The modern observance is an unofficial pet-lover holiday.
holidays.funFact: Spratt's meat-fibrin dog cakes launched the commercial pet food industry, which is now worth well over a hundred billion dollars worldwide.

holidays.name: International Tug of War Day
holidays.description: A day for pulling, grunting, and digging your heels into the ground in the name of rope-based glory. Teams gather to remind the world that sometimes the simplest games are the most dramatic.
holidays.origin: Tug of war is an ancient contest with roots in China, Egypt, and Greece, and it was an official Olympic event from 1900 to 1920. The date is a modern, unofficial observance celebrating the sport's history.
holidays.funFact: Tug of war was once an Olympic event, and in 1908 a dispute broke out when the US team accused the British police team of wearing illegal boots with steel cleats.

holidays.name: Digital Learning Day
holidays.description: A day when educators and students celebrate technology in the classroom, from coding lessons to virtual field trips to the surface of Mars. Chalkboards everywhere pretend not to be jealous.
holidays.origin: Digital Learning Day began in 2012 as a national campaign by the Alliance for Excellent Education to spotlight effective uses of technology in teaching, and it grew into an annual event with thousands of schools participating.
holidays.funFact: The first Digital Learning Day featured a live broadcast of education leaders and celebrity guests, and schools in all 50 U.S. states took part in the celebration.

holidays.name: Curling Is Cool Day
holidays.description: A salute to the sport where people frantically sweep ice in front of a sliding granite stone while shouting commands at it. It is equal parts chess, shuffleboard, and housekeeping on ice.
holidays.origin: Curling dates back to 16th-century Scotland, and a sporting tradition has spread worldwide through winter Olympics broadcasts that turn millions of viewers into overnight armchair experts. The day is an informal fan-driven observance during the winter sports season.
holidays.funFact: A curling stone weighs roughly 42 pounds, and the granite used for the finest stones traditionally comes from a single Scottish island called Ailsa Craig.
